_comment: TODO: Populate with labeled ground-truth bugs for the seeded_bugs/ samples. Each entry should describe the file, the seeded bug's location/type, and whether it is actually a bug.

_schema_example.id: string - unique id matching a file in seeded_bugs/
_schema_example.is_bug: boolean - whether this sample actually contains a bug
_schema_example.bug_type: string - e.g. 'off-by-one', 'null-deref', 'sql-injection', or null if not a bug
_schema_example.line: integer|null - line number of the bug, if applicable
_schema_example.description: string - short human description of the bug
_schema_example.source: string - 'synthetic' (hand-written for this project) or 'real_world' (adapted from a real CVE/issue/commit)
_schema_example.citation: string|null - source citation for real_world entries (CVE id, issue link, etc.), null for synthetic

bugs.description: Off-by-one: `end = start + page_size + 1` includes one extra item, so each page overlaps the next page by one item.
Off-by-one: `range(len(values) - window)` stops one iteration short, so the moving average silently drops the last valid window.
Off-by-one: `range(0, len(items) - 1, batch_size)` can exclude a valid starting index at `len(items) - 1`, silently dropping the last chunk of items.
Wrong comparison operator: uses `>` instead of `<=`, so batteries above the low-battery threshold are reported as low and batteries at or below it are not.
Wrong comparison operator: uses `<=` instead of `>=`, so orders under the free-shipping threshold ship free while orders that actually qualify are charged.
Wrong comparison operator: the 'C' branch uses `>` instead of `>=`, so a score of exactly 70 incorrectly falls through to grade 'D'.
Incorrect boundary condition: loop uses `low < high` instead of `low <= high`, so the search misses the target when it is the last remaining candidate.
Incorrect boundary condition: uses `length <= MIN_LENGTH` instead of `length < MIN_LENGTH`, so a password exactly at the minimum length is incorrectly rejected.
Bad state handling: `cart=[]` is a mutable default argument, so the same list is reused and accumulates items across unrelated calls to `add_item`.
Bad state handling: `reset_on_success` is a no-op (`pass`), so `attempts` is never reset and a tracker that already succeeded still reports exhausted retries afterward.
SQL injection: the query string is built with `%` string formatting on `username` instead of a parameterized query, so a crafted username can alter the SQL statement.
Command injection: `hostname` is concatenated directly into a shell command passed to `os.system`, so a crafted hostname (e.g. containing `;`) can execute arbitrary shell commands.
Hardcoded secret: `SECRET_KEY` is a literal string committed in source rather than loaded from an environment variable or secret manager, exposing the signing key to anyone with source access.
Insecure deserialization: `pickle.loads` is called on `raw_cookie_value`, which comes from a client-controlled cookie; a crafted pickle payload can execute arbitrary code.
Weak cryptography: passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5, which is fast to brute-force and unsuitable for password storage; should use a slow, salted algorithm like bcrypt or scrypt.
Bare except clause: `except:` catches every exception (including KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit), silently masking bugs unrelated to int parsing.
Shadowed builtin: the local variable `dict` shadows the builtin `dict` type within the function, which is confusing and error-prone if the constructor is needed later in scope.
Unused variable: `tax` is computed but never added to the total or included in the receipt output, so the computation is dead code and the receipt silently omits tax.

Singleton comparison: `user["active"] == True` should be a plain truthy check; as written it silently excludes active users whose `active` field is truthy but not the literal `True` (e.g. a non-boolean truthy value).

Inconsistent return statements: there is no `else`/default branch, so an unrecognized `customer_tier` causes the function to implicitly return `None`, which later crashes `apply_discount`'s arithmetic.
Path traversal: `archive.extractall(destination_dir)` doesn't validate member paths, so a crafted tar archive with '../' entries can write files outside destination_dir.
bugs.citation: CVE-2007-4559 — Python tarfile extractall() path traversal, affecting an estimated 350,000+ open-source projects (Trellix, 2022).

bugs.description: Insecure deserialization: `yaml.load(config_text)` without a safe loader can construct and execute arbitrary Python objects from the YAML input.
bugs.citation: CVE-2017-18342 — PyYAML yaml.load() arbitrary code execution (fixed by making yaml.safe_load() / an explicit Loader the required interface).

bugs.description: Header/CRLF injection: `search_term` is concatenated directly into the URL without rejecting \r\n sequences, letting a crafted search term inject extra HTTP headers into the outgoing request.
bugs.citation: CVE-2019-9947 — CRLF/header injection in Python's urllib due to insufficient validation of URL components (bpo-35906).

bugs.description: Open redirect: checking only `target_url.startswith("/")` treats protocol-relative URLs like '//evil.com' as safe, but browsers resolve them as absolute URLs to the attacker's site.
bugs.citation: CVE-2014-3730 — Django is_safe_url() open redirect via insufficiently validated redirect targets.

bugs.description: Off-by-one: an extra `chunks_read += 1` after the loop over-counts by one, reporting one more chunk read than actually occurred.
bugs.citation: Documented off-by-one in Python's stdlib urllib.URLopener.retrieve(), which reported reading one more block than it actually read.

bugs.description: Off-by-one: `duration_days` returns `(end - start).days`, which excludes the end date even though the class is documented as inclusive of both endpoints (e.g. Jan 1 to Jan 1 should span 1 day, not 0).
bugs.citation: Real off-by-one bug fixed in octoenergy/xocto PR #98 — a FiniteDateRange property returned a value exclusive of the end date despite the range being double-inclusive.

bugs.description: Off-by-one in negative-step slice bounds: when `n == len(items)`, `stop = len(items) - n - 1` evaluates to -1, which Python re-interprets as index `len(items) - 1` rather than "before index 0", so the full-length case silently returns an empty list instead of everything reversed.
bugs.citation: Adapted from pandas-dev/pandas PR #55832 (merged Nov 2023) — a real off-by-one in negative-step slice boundary handling for PyArrow-backed arrays, simplified here into pure-Python list slicing.

bugs.description: Bad state handling: `agent_input: dict = {}` is a mutable default argument, so the same dict is reused and accumulates history across unrelated calls to `add_memory`.
bugs.citation: Exact bug pattern from agentuniverse-ai/agentUniverse GitHub Issue #1184 — three agent-memory methods declared mutable dict defaults, causing cross-call state pollution in long-running agent processes.

bugs.description: Bare except clause: `except:` catches every exception including SystemExit and KeyboardInterrupt, so a plugin that calls sys.exit() during import is silently treated as "failed to load" instead of actually exiting.
bugs.citation: Well-documented real-world anti-pattern (Pylint's own W0702 'bare-except' rule exists because of recurring incidents like this; no single canonical commit cited).

bugs.description: Security check via `assert`: Python strips all assert statements when run with the -O optimization flag, so this authorization check silently disappears in an optimized production deployment.
bugs.citation: CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion) / Bandit rule B101 — using assert for security or business-logic validation is a well-documented real-world anti-pattern, distinct from any single CVE.
